items.informal_name: Compatibility of Multivariate Polynomial Evaluation with Ring Homomorphism Composition
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S₁ : Type v} {S₂ : Type w} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S₁]
  [inst_2 : CommSemiring S₂] (f : R →+* S₁) (g : σ → S₁) (φ : S₁ →+* S₂) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  φ ((MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom f g) p) = (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom (φ.comp f) fun i => φ (g i)) p
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $R$, type $\sigma$, and ring homomorphisms $f : R \to S_1$, $g : \sigma \to S_1$, and $\phi : S_1 \to S_2$, the evaluation of a polynomial $p \in R[\sigma]$ satisfies $\phi(\mathrm{eval}_2(f, g, p)) = \mathrm{eval}_2(\phi \circ f, \phi \circ g, p)$. This expresses that applying $\phi$ after evaluation is equivalent to composing $\phi$ with the coefficient map and variable assignment before evaluation.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Evaluation and Coefficient Mapping in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S₁ : Type v} {S₂ : Type w} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S₁]
  [inst_2 : CommSemiring S₂] (f : R →+* S₁) (g : σ → S₂) (φ : S₁ →+* S₂) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom φ g) ((MvPolynomial.map f) p) = (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom (φ.comp f) g) p
items.informal_description: For commutative semirings $R$, $S_1$, $S_2$, a type $\sigma$, ring homomorphism $f : R \to S_1$, variable assignment $g : \sigma \to S_2$, and ring homomorphism $\phi : S_1 \to S_2$, the evaluation of the polynomial $\mathrm{map}\,f\,p$ using $\phi$ and $g$ equals the evaluation of $p$ using the composed homomorphism $\phi \circ f$ and $g$. Formally, $\mathrm{eval}_2\,\phi\,g\, (\mathrm{map}\,f\,p) = \mathrm{eval}_2\, (\phi \circ f)\,g\,p$ for all $p \in R[\sigma]$.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Multivariate Polynomial Evaluation with Coefficient Mapping
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S₁ : Type v} {S₂ : Type w} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S₁]
  [inst_2 : CommSemiring S₂] (f : R →+* S₁) (g : σ → S₂) (φ : S₁ →+* S₂) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  MvPolynomial.eval₂ φ g ((MvPolynomial.map f) p) = MvPolynomial.eval₂ (φ.comp f) g p
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $R$, type $\sigma$, and commutative semirings $S_1, S_2$, given a ring homomorphism $f : R \to S_1$, a variable assignment $g : \sigma \to S_2$, and a ring homomorphism $\phi : S_1 \to S_2$, the evaluation of the polynomial $\mathrm{map}\, f\, p$ using coefficient map $\phi$ and variable map $g$ equals the evaluation of $p$ using the composed coefficient map $\phi \circ f$ and variable map $g$. Formally, $\mathrm{eval}_2(\phi, g, \mathrm{map}\, f\, p) = \mathrm{eval}_2(\phi \circ f, g, p)$ for all $p \in R[\sigma]$.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Multivariate Polynomial Evaluation with Composed Ring Homomorphisms
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $S_2$, ring homomorphism $k : S_1 \to S_2$, ring homomorphism $f : R \to S_1$, variable assignment $g : \sigma \to S_1$, and polynomial $p$, applying $k$ to the evaluation of $p$ using $f$ on coefficients and $g$ on variables equals evaluating the polynomial $\mathrm{map}\,f\,p$ using $k \circ g$ on variables and $k$ on coefficients. Formally: $k(\mathrm{eval}_2\,f\,g\,p) = \mathrm{eval}_2\,k\,(k \circ g)\,(\mathrm{map}\,f\,p)$.

items.informal_name: Evaluation of Multivariate Polynomials Composes with Ring Homomorphisms
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S₁ : Type v} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S₁] (f : R →+* S₁)
  (g : σ → R) (p : MvPolynomial σ R), f ((MvPolynomial.eval g) p) = MvPolynomial.eval₂ f (⇑f ∘ g) p
items.informal_description: For any ring homomorphism $ f : R \to S_1 $, any map $ g : \sigma \to R $, and any polynomial $ p \in R[\sigma] $, it holds that $ f(\mathrm{eval}_g(p)) = \mathrm{eval}_{f, f \circ g}(p) $, where $ \mathrm{eval}_g $ denotes evaluation using variable map $ g $ and identity coefficient map, and $ \mathrm{eval}_{f, f \circ g} $ denotes evaluation using coefficient map $ f $ and variable map $ f \circ g $.
